body:
Source: GitHub issues #779 (bug, P1-high, class data loss) and #782 (bug, P1-high, class false-green). Re-verified on main @ a627e4ac.

DEFECT A (#779) — packages/ticket-prune/lib/detect.mjs:68. `return scope.every((glob) => trackedFiles.some((file) => globMatch(glob, file)));`. `scopeShipped()` calls a ticket shipped when every declared `scope` glob resolves to at least one file tracked at the base ref. On any repo older than its ticket backlog this is true the instant a ticket is authored: a ticket scoped to `packages/core/**` matches because `packages/core/` already exists, not because the ticket's work landed. There is no check that the scope files changed, that they were created by the ticket, or that the ticket ever entered a build. classifyTicket (detect.mjs:91-97) turns that into `stale: true, reason: 'inferred: all N declared scope glob(s) resolve to tracked files on the base ref'`. Measured on this repo at the time of filing: 179 of 206 tickets classified STALE, 23 of them tombstone-eligible (no `completed` field, no rails) and therefore archived by `ticket-prune --write` — every one of the 23 OPEN work that had never been completed. The run reports `ok: true`, exits 0, and prints `Archived 23 rails-less stale ticket(s) out of the active directory store`, so nothing in the output signals that the live backlog was just removed. Recovery exists (shards are retained under `.adlc/ticket-archive/` and restoreTicket can put them back), but the operator has to notice first.

DEFECT B (#782) — docs/ci/adlc-maintenance.yml:112. `if [ -f .adlc/tickets.json ]; then`. That file is the ready-to-use scheduled workflow the README and /adlc-maintain point operators at, and its ticket-prune step guards on the presence of the LEGACY flat file. A repo on the canonical sharded backend has no `.adlc/tickets.json` — the store is `.adlc/tickets/.store.json` plus the shards beside it — so the guard is false, `rc=0` is forced, the summary prints `(.adlc/tickets.json not present — nothing to prune)` (:118), and the check never runs. The step is green having examined nothing. This is the opposite of what the tool does: `loadTickets()` in @adlc/core falls back to DirectoryTicketStore when the flat file is absent, so ticket-prune would have worked fine had the guard let it run. Since new repos default to sharded, the shipped recipe is a no-op for most installs that copy it.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/ticket-prune` (an npm workspace). Modules: `bin/ticket-prune.mjs` (parseArgs at :34-44 — currently `tickets`, `base-ref`, `write`, `ceremony`, `json`, `allow-unsigned`; manifest-key resolution and the unsigned warning follow); `lib/detect.mjs` (listTrackedFiles, explicitStatus, isExplicitlyDone, scopeShipped, classifyTicket, classifyTickets, and the disposition helper that decides done / tombstone / ceremony); `lib/run.mjs` (runTicketPrune — the library entry point); `lib/store.mjs`; `lib/archive-order.mjs`; `lib/format.mjs`. Tests: `npm test -w packages/ticket-prune` from the worktree root, or `node scripts/run-tests.mjs ticket-prune`. Existing tests that are NOT rails and MAY be changed: `test/roundtrip.test.mjs` (see the next paragraph), `test/detect.test.mjs` and `test/run.test.mjs` (both currently pin the always-on inference — rewrite what pins the bug and say so in the PR body), `test/active-completed.test.mjs`, `test/format.test.mjs`, `test/wedge-fix.test.mjs`, `test/list-tracked-files.test.mjs`.

RAIL CORRECTION (ticket amended after the build began). `packages/ticket-prune/test/roundtrip.test.mjs` was originally declared a rail. That was WRONG and the rail has been dropped: the file drives the real CLI over fixtures whose staleness comes ONLY from the scope inference (`scope: ['plugins/adlc-widget/**']` with no `status` field), so with the inference correctly defaulted off nothing is stale, `--write` tombstones nothing, and three of its tests fail. It is a test that pins the bug, which the rail rules forbid railing. The ONLY change it needs is three argv arrays — add `'--infer-scope'` before `'--write'` at :47 (`[PRUNE_BIN, '--write']`), at :140 and at :185 (`[PRUNE_BIN, '--write', '--json']`). No assertion in that file changes. This was verified empirically on a throwaway copy: with exactly those three edits the file passes 5/5.

CRITICAL CONSUMER CONSTRAINT — read before designing. `scripts/ceremony-drift.mjs:652` calls `runTicketPrune({ cwd: process.cwd(), baseRef: process.env.BASE_REF || 'origin/main' })` and reports on the `needsCeremony` set that only exists downstream of a ticket being classified STALE. If the inference defaults off and ceremony-drift is not updated, that reporter silently stops finding drift — a second false-green introduced by this fix. It MUST be updated to pass the inference explicitly so its behaviour is byte-identical to today. Its guards `scripts/test/ceremony-drift.test.mjs` and `scripts/test/ceremony-command-safety.test.mjs` must stay green. Note that `packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/rail-freeze.mjs` and the three `active-tickets.mjs` enumerators only reference the `completed: true` marker ticket-prune writes, not this inference, so they are unaffected — verify that rather than assuming it.

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. The scope-existence inference becomes opt-in, threaded as ONE named option with the same spelling at every level: `inferScope` (boolean, DEFAULT FALSE) on `classifyTicket(ticket, trackedFiles, { inferScope = false } = {})`, `classifyTickets(tickets, trackedFiles, { inferScope = false } = {})` and `runTicketPrune({ …, inferScope = false })`; surfaced on the CLI as `--infer-scope` (boolean, default false).
2. With `inferScope` false, a ticket with no explicit status is NEVER inferred stale, regardless of its scope. Its classification becomes `stale: false` with the reason `no explicit status; scope-existence inference is off (pass --infer-scope to enable it)`. A ticket WITH an explicit done-shaped status is unaffected — `explicitStatus`/`isExplicitlyDone` keep deciding it exactly as today.
3. With `inferScope` true, behaviour is byte-identical to today, including the existing reason string `inferred: all N declared scope glob(s) resolve to tracked files on the base ref`. `scopeShipped()` itself is unchanged.
4. `scripts/ceremony-drift.mjs` passes `inferScope: true` in its runTicketPrune call so its drift set is unchanged. Add a one-line comment saying why (its job is to surface shipped-but-uncompleted rail-freezing tickets, which is exactly what the inference is for) and that whether that inference is trustworthy for ceremony-drift is tracked separately.
5. The CLI's dry-run and `--json` output must make the mode visible: the report states whether scope-existence inference was on or off, and `--json` carries `inferScope` (boolean). An operator reading either output can tell which classifier produced the counts.
6. `docs/ci/adlc-maintenance.yml` — replace the legacy-only guard at :112 with one that covers both backends (`[ -f .adlc/tickets.json ] || [ -f .adlc/tickets/.store.json ]`), and update the skip message at :118 so it names both paths. Do not add `--write` or `--infer-scope` to the recipe: it stays report-only, exactly as today.
7. Regression guard, must keep behaving exactly as today: `--write` still requires the tombstone/ceremony disposition logic unchanged; the `--allow-unsigned` warning and the manifest-key handling are untouched; `--ceremony` output is unchanged; archive/restore ordering is unchanged; a ticket with no declared scope is still 'no explicit status and no declared scope — cannot infer, treated as active'.
8. Documentation: describe `--infer-scope`, the new default, and WHY (scope existence is not evidence that the ticket's work landed — it is true the moment the ticket is authored on any repo older than its backlog) in `packages/ticket-prune/README.md`, and make the SAME edits by hand in `docs/tools/ticket-prune.md` and `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/ticket-prune.mdx` (hand-maintained mirrors — never regenerate).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 With inference off (the default), a ticket with no explicit status and a scope whose globs all resolve to tracked files classifies `stale: false` with the new reason. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/infer-scope-gate.test.mjs`
- AC2 With `inferScope: true` the same ticket classifies `stale: true` with the original reason string, unchanged. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/infer-scope-gate.test.mjs`
- AC3 A ticket with an explicit done-shaped status classifies stale in BOTH modes; a ticket with no scope classifies active in both. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/infer-scope-gate.test.mjs`
- AC4 `runTicketPrune` with no options archives nothing that only the inference marked stale; the same call with `inferScope: true` reproduces today's set. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/infer-scope-gate.test.mjs`
- AC5 The CLI accepts `--infer-scope`, and `--json` carries `inferScope` reflecting the flag. verify: `node --test packages/ticket-prune/test/infer-scope-gate.test.mjs`
- AC6 The shipped CI recipe's guard is true for a sharded store. verify: `grep -c 'tickets/.store.json' docs/ci/adlc-maintenance.yml` (>= 1) and `node --test scripts/test/ceremony-command-safety.test.mjs`
- AC7 ceremony-drift's drift set is unchanged. verify: `node --test scripts/test/ceremony-drift.test.mjs`
- AC8 Existing package suite green, including the rewritten assertions in test/detect.test.mjs and test/run.test.mjs and the three argv additions in test/roundtrip.test.mjs. verify: `npm test -w packages/ticket-prune`
- AC9 Docs updated in all three places. verify: `grep -c infer-scope packages/ticket-prune/README.md docs/tools/ticket-prune.md apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/ticket-prune.mdx` (each >= 1)
- AC10 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: adding a `--yes` confirmation to `--write` (the inference gate is the fix; a confirmation prompt would change the documented /adlc-maintain flow); corroborating shipped-ness against the ticket's creation revision or git history; changing what ceremony-drift infers; changing the archive/restore format; touching lib/store.mjs or lib/archive-order.mjs.
title: ticket-prune: gate scope-existence staleness behind --infer-scope, and make the shipped CI recipe see a sharded store
